verdict.rationale: Svelte ships an official, documented `sv` CLI. It can scaffold projects (`sv create`, with templates such as `library` and a choice of package manager), add functionality to existing projects (`sv add`, including local add-ons), check code for errors and warnings (`sv check`), and convert playground URLs into full SvelteKit projects. The CLI docs are also published in LLM-consumable llms.txt form. missing for 10: evidence of agent-oriented CLI behavior (non-interactive or machine-readable output modes), independent or hands-on corroboration of CLI use in AI workflows.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can use an official CLI

citations.quote: The easiest way to start building a SvelteKit app is to run `npx sv create`
`sv add` updates an existing project with new functionality.
`sv check` finds errors and warnings in your project, such as: unused CSS, accessibility hints, JavaScript/TypeScript compiler errors
Create a SvelteKit project from a playground URL. This downloads all playground files, detects external dependencies, and sets up a complete SvelteKit project structure
Installs dependencies with a specified package manager: npm, pnpm, yarn, bun, deno
